The motivation behind the project was to address the challenges faced by companies, such as difficulty in extracting information from documents, the time- consuming process of manually extracting information, and the need for efficient storage and retrieval of data. The system aims to automate the extraction of information f rom documents such as invoices and convert them into electronically archived data, which can be accessed easily and quickly. A hybrid approach of machine learning and human interaction is also implemented to match extracted ite

ces and convert them into electronically archived data, which can be accessed easily and quickly. A hybrid approach of machine learning and human interaction is also implemented to match extracted items from invoices with items i n the database. The system was develo ped using cloud technology, specifically Google Cloud, to take advantage of its scalability, reliability, and security features. The implementation of cloud technology also allows for easy and cost-effective storage of large amounts of data. The results of the project showed that the system was able to successfully extract information from invoices and accurately match items with the database, significantly reducing the time and effort required for manual extraction. In conclusion, the document extraction a nd archiving system utilizing Google C loud technology represent a significant step forward in addressing the challenges faced by companies in managing and accessing their data. The implementati on of the hybrid approach and the use of cloud technology has p roven to be effective in improving the efficiency and accuracy of the extraction and archiving process. Through the integration with Google Filament, the framework ensured that 3D graphics were not only realistic but also beautifully rendered, featuring accurate lighting and shadows to enhance user experience. In this setup, various components were declared and utilized as follows: a reference to the ArFragment was established for AR functionalities, named `arFragment`. Access to the SceneView and the Scene for rendering AR content was provided through `arSceneView` and `scene`, respectively. The 3D model (Renderable) and its UI view (ViewRenderable) were held by `model` and `modelView`, accordingly. The method `loadModels` was employed to asynchronously load the 3D model and its view using ModelRenderable.builder() and ViewRenderable.builder(). Furthermore, the method `onTapPlane` was designed to handle user taps on de

was employed to asynchronously load the 3D model and its view using ModelRenderable.builder() and ViewRenderable.builder(). Furthermore, the method `onTapPlane` was designed to handle user taps on detected planes by creating an anchor, adding a Transformable Node for the 3D model, and configuring the model's properties and position. Key concepts and technologies such as ARCore, Google's AR platform, and Sceneform, a 3D framework for adding AR content which simplifies 3D scene rendering, were central to this implementation. Additionally, Renderables represented 3D models and 2D UI elements in the AR scene, while Nodes and Anchors organized 3D objects in the scene, with Anchors linking virtual content to real-world positions for stability as the user moves. 6. AR Measuring To measure a distance using augmented reality (AR), the user is supposed to be in the augmented reality interface and given permission to access the camera. Augmented reality detects space and shows points on space. The user starts by picking two points. A line is drawn between these points, and the distance is calculated using this formula (sqrt((x2 - x1)^2 + (y2 - y1)^2 + (z2 - z1)^2)) that considers the positio

he user starts by picking two points. A line is drawn between these points, and the distance is calculated using this formula (sqrt((x2 - x1)^2 + (y2 - y1)^2 + (z2 - z1)^2)) that considers the positions of these points in three dimensions. The measurement's accuracy depends on these factors: AR efficiency: The better the augmented reality technology, the more accurate the measurements. User awareness: The accuracy also depends on how the user picks the points to be measured, Careless point placement causes errors. Environment Visibility: lighting affects how accurately it can measure distances. Camera resolution and clarity. With high-quality AR devices and proper lighting, the error rate can be as low as 1% per meter, which leads to an error of up to 2 cm. However, with lower-quality devices and poor conditions, errors may rise to 4% per meter. 45 7. Firebase Firebase Auth is used to manage accounts, including registration and login. The following are the eight types of tests we conducted on the project: 63 - Unit Testing:  Purpose: To test individual units or components of the software application.  Method: Developers write tests for each function or module; these tests are run every time the code changes to ensure that no new errors have been introduced. - Integration Testing:  Purpose: To expose faults in the interaction between integrated units.  Method: Combining individual software modules and testing them as a group, often using techniques like top-down, bottom- up, and sandwich testing. - System Testing:  Purpose: To validate the software as a whole and ensure

vidual software modules and testing them as a group, often using techniques like top-down, bottom- up, and sandwich testing. - System Testing:  Purpose: To validate the software as a whole and ensure it meets the specified requirements.  Method: Conducted on a complete, integrated system to evaluate the system's compliance with its specified requirements. - User Acceptance Testing (UAT):  Purpose: To determine if the system satisfies the business needs and requirements.  Method: Typically performed by the end-users to ensure the software can handle required tasks in real-world scenarios, often following real-world usage scenarios. - Performance Testing:  Purpose: To test the behaviour of the system under certain conditions.  Method: Involves load testing (determining how the system behaves under heavy loads) and stress testing (how the system behaves under extreme conditions). - Security Testing:  Purpose: To identify any weaknesses, vulnerabilities, or threats in the software.  Method: Includes tests like penetration testing, vulnerability scanning, and risk assessment. - Compatibility Testing:  Purpose: To check the compatibility of the software with different environmen

 Method: Includes tests like penetration testing, vulnerability scanning, and risk assessment. - Compatibility Testing:  Purpose: To check the compatibility of the software with different environments.  Method: Testing how the software operates in various environments, including different web browsers, database versions, hardware, operating systems, mobile devices, and network environments. 64 - Regression Testing:  Purpose: To ensure that recent code changes haven't adversely affected existing features.  Method: Re-running previously passed tests on new software versions to check that existing functionality remains unaffected by new development. 10. natural language processing (NLP), named entity recognition (NER) is a critical foundational task. NER involves identifying specific words or phrases in unstructured text—such as individual names, locations, and organizations—and categorizing them into predefined groups. This capability is essential for various NLP tasks including machine translation, question answering, entity linking, and relation extraction. These situations give rise to what is known as nested entities or entity nesting. Such complexities are prevalent in specific domain-oriented datasets. While most research has focused on resolving flat entities, the challenges posed by nested entities often remain unaddressed. Named Entity Recognition serves as a bridge between unstructured text and structured data, enabling machines to sift through vast amounts of textual information and extract valuable data in categorized forms. News feed retrieval and content categorization utilizing Natural Language Processing (NLP) methods are the two primary project functionalities. In the realm of bioinformatics and computational biology, the selection of appropriate feature extraction methods is crucial for the success of predictive models. Binary Profile Features (BPF) and K-mer Matrix are often chosen due to their effectiveness in capturing essential sequence information. Here, we provide a detailed rationale for selecting these two features for sequence prediction tasks. Binary Profile Features (BPF) Binary Profile Features offer a simple and intuitive representation of sequences. Each amino acid or nucleotide is encoded as a binary vector, providing a straightforward way to capture the presence or absence of specific residues or properties. This method is versatile, allowing adaptation to various sequence properties such as structural motifs or functional domains. Furthermore, the computational efficiency of binary vectors facilitates rapid similarity calculations and is well-suited for machine learning algorithms requiring fixed-length input vectors. Additionally

thermore, the computational efficiency of binary vectors facilitates rapid similarity calculations and is well-suited for machine learning algorithms requiring fixed-length input vectors. Additionally, BPF is particularly effective for tasks involving sequence alignment and comparison, quickly highlighting similarities and differences between sequences. K-mer Matrix The K-mer Matrix method captures rich sequence information by representing sequences as overlapping subsequences of length kkk. This approach provides a comprehensive view of both local and global sequence contexts. The flexibility of adjusting the k-mer length allows for capturing varying degrees of sequence details, with short k-mers focusing on local features and longer k-mers encompassing extended sequence patterns. K-mers have been demonstrated to enhance prediction accuracy across various bioinformatics applications, including motif discovery, sequence alignment, and classification. Their . 96 applicability to DNA, RNA, and protein sequences makes k-mers a universal feature extraction method. recognize relationships between vast amounts of data. They consist of layers of interconnected nodes or neurons, where each node represents a mathematical function. Key components • Input Layer: Receives the input data (features). • Hidden Layers: Intermediate layers that process the input data, consisting of neurons that apply transformations and pass the data to the next layer. • Output Layer: Produces the final output (predictions). Dense layers In the context of our model, it primarily focuses on the use of Dense layers, which are fully connected layers where each neuron is connected to every neuron in the previous and next layers. Some key features include: • Activation Functions: functions applied to each neuron introduce non-linearities into the model, helping it learn complex patterns. Common activation functions include ReLU (Rectified Linear Unit) for hidden layers and softmax for the output layer in classification tasks. • Dropout: A regularization technique used to prevent overfitting by randomly setting a fraction of input units to 0 at each update during training. Softmax Activation For the output layer, the softmax activation function is used. This function converts the raw prediction scores (logits) into probabilities, with the sum of all probabilities equal to 100%.
